issues.legal_issue: A later procedural restriction on second appeals does not remove a vested right of appeal in a pending suit unless the later law expressly or by necessary implication makes that restriction applicable.
material_facts: The suit was instituted when the procedural code then governing it allowed a second appeal on questions of fact as well as law.
After the suit was instituted, a different procedural code was extended to the territory and restricted the High Court’s second-appeal jurisdiction.
The later legislation contained no express provision, or necessary implication, applying that restriction retrospectively.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s jurisdiction in the second appeal continued to be governed by the earlier procedural code, and the later restriction applied only to suits instituted after it took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Procedural changes are generally retrospective, but a right of appeal is a substantive vested right governed by the law in force when the suit is commenced. That right includes successive appeals in the same proceeding and may be taken away only expressly or by necessary implication. The Court relied on Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving, Delhi Cloth and General Mills Co. Ltd. v. Income-tax Commissioner, and Garikapatti Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhury.

rule.if: second_appeal_from_trial_decree and suit_began_under_broader_appeal_right and later_law_restricted_appeals and not later_law_made_restriction_retroactive

predicates.second_appeal_from_trial_decree: The proceeding is a second appeal from a decree made in a first appeal.
predicates.suit_began_under_broader_appeal_right: The suit began when the governing law allowed a second appeal on questions of fact as well as law.
predicates.later_law_restricted_appeals: A later law restricted the scope of second appeals.
predicates.not later_law_made_restriction_retroacti: The later law did not expressly or by necessary implication apply its restriction to suits already pending.

issues.definition: When a second appeal arises from a suit begun under a broader appeal right, a later restriction that does not apply retrospectively leaves that earlier appeal jurisdiction in place.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court ordinarily does not disturb a High Court’s factual finding in a special-leave appeal when the High Court was competent to decide the facts and the finding has support in the evidence.
material_facts: The trial court found that the daughter had died before the limited owner, relying on witness evidence and a revenue record that supported its conclusion.
The first appellate court reached the opposite conclusion without discussing the parties’ evidence in detail, relying in part on the absence of a statement that the daughter had inherited the land.
The High Court preferred the trial court’s view of the evidence and found that the daughter had died first.
The appeal to the Supreme Court was brought by special leave, and the High Court had jurisdiction to decide factual questions in the second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to disturb the High Court’s finding that the daughter had predeceased the limited owner and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal by special leave under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court will not ordinarily discard a High Court’s finding on a question of fact when the High Court was competent under the law governing the appeal to reach that finding. The Court also rejected the inference drawn by the first appellate court from the witnesses’ failure to say that the daughter inherited the property.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and challenged_finding_is_factual and high_court_was_competent_to_decide_facts and evidence_supports_high_court_finding

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding before the Supreme Court is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.challenged_finding_is_factual: The finding challenged in the appeal concerns a question of fact.
predicates.high_court_was_competent_to_decide_facts: The High Court had authority under the law governing the appeal to decide the factual question.
predicates.evidence_supports_high_court_finding: The evidence in the record provides support for the High Court’s factual finding.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges a factual finding that the High Court was competent to make and that the evidence supports, the Supreme Court ordinarily leaves that finding undisturbed.
